Weight savings of up to 80 percent can be achieved by switching from aluminum EMI shielding covers to intercalated graphite fiber composites.
Intercalated graphite fibers have mechanical and thermal properties nearly identical to pristine graphite fibers.
The resistivity of intercalated graphite fibers is lower by a factor of 5 compared to stainless steel.
Intercalated graphite fiber composites have a much higher specific strength than aluminum.
The composites absorb and reradiate electromagnetic radiation in the infrared region, making them better at rejecting heat.
The number of electrons in an atom affects radiation shielding, with more electrons resulting in better shielding.
Intercalation with bromine or iodine improves radiation shielding in graphite fibers.
The actual improvement in radiation shielding observed in the study was a factor of 8 over pristine graphite composite, and a factor of 3 over aluminum.
Intercalated graphite composites may be the EMI cover of choice for spacecraft electronics operating in high-radiation environments.
